prompt: A patio is $(x + 5)$ meters long and $(x - 2)$ meters wide. Multiply to write its area.
hint: Multiply length by width as with any rectangle. One of the numbers is negative, so carry its sign through each product.

hints.text: Multiply length by width as with any rectangle. One of the numbers is negative, so carry its sign through each product.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $(x + 2)(x - 1)$: that is $x^2 - x + 2x - 2 = x^2 + x - 2$. Multiply all four pairs, then combine.
The four products are $x \times x = x^2$, $x \times (-2) = -2x$, $5 \times x = 5x$ and $5 \times (-2) = -10$. Add them and combine the middle terms.
$x^2 - 2x + 5x - 10$ combines to give an area of $x^2 + 3x - 10$ square meters.

explanation: Distribute each term of the first bracket over the second: $(x + 5)(x - 2) = x(x - 2) + 5(x - 2)$.
Multiplying out each part, with the signs kept, gives $x^2 - 2x + 5x - 10$.
The two middle terms are like terms, so combine them: $-2x + 5x = 3x$.
The area of the patio is $x^2 + 3x - 10$ square meters.

alternativeExplanations.title: Area model with a sign
steps: Split the rectangle into 4 patches, labeling the width pieces x and −2.
Patch areas: x², −2x, 5x, −10 — the negative pieces are area being trimmed off.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with x = 4
steps: At x = 4 the patio is 9 m by 2 m, so the area is 18 square meters.
The formula: 16 + 12 − 10 = 18. The expansion is correct.
